messages:
alina: Noticed canary for 'sable-lite-int8' PTQ bring-up has parse failures up to 1.9%. Failures are mostly funcall malformats and occasional plaintext suffixes.

rick: Onboard or prod canary?

alina: Onboard canary ensemble. Baseline float was ~0.2%. Ran the standard structured-eval harness.

pavan: Any small failing examples we can paste?

alina: Example redacted:
{
  "req": "u23",
  "tool_call": "run_task(name=fetch_user, id=42)"
}
Here tool_call is a text blob instead of object. Others have trailing plaintext like "
OK".

erin: That smells like token boundary merging or stream reassembly glitch under batching. Any signal with batch_size or concurrent streams?

alina: Telemetry: spikes correlate with batch_size>=6 and concurrent_streams>=3. Single-playback often succeeds.

rick: Can we capture raw token stream + token offsets for failures and request logits for a sample set?

pavan: Yes, request logits + top-k token boundaries for 20 failures. Also enable a strict-json-wrapper to record raw byte stream for any parse failures.

erin: Short-term mitigation: push an output sanitizer in the canary middleware to coerce common text blobs into the expected object (log original + sanitized). That preserves downstream behavior while we debug. Metric sanitizer rate.

alina: Agreed. Plan: 1) sweep batch_size=[1,2,4,6,8] x concurrent_streams=[1..4]; 2) enable token-offset tracing on failures; 3) deploy sanitizer and monitor sanitizer_rate.

rick: I'll flip ensemble fallback off for this model in the canary routing while we run experiments.

triage-bot: Created INC-3229: "sable-lite-int8 PTQ canary parse spike" assigned to @alina and @rick, severity S2.

pavan: If we see strong batch sensitivity, consider an autoscaler guard that caps per-GPU batch size for the canary. Also check if int4 variants show the same behavior.

alina: Kicked off the sweep, uploading a tiny repro gist when available. Will post 1-2 minimal repros here. :thumbsup:
